solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Much nationwide suffering after revolution spread

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the hidden letters are read from right to left
much of the phrase, not all of it, is used, so the letters sit inside the run of words

parts.note: sitting across the end of nationwide and the start of suffering

explanation.surface: A news report that widespread national hardship followed an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the hidden run backwards to get EFFUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Effused means poured out or diffused, so a liquid or feeling that has effused has spread.

clue.text: Slips out of shop in time

indicators.note: one word placed in another means the second wraps around the first

parts.note: an era is a period of time
to rat or shop someone is to inform on them

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks out of a store just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slips out' looks like one verb phrase, but 'Slips' alone is the definition and 'shop' is a verb meaning betray, as in informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed mistakes in a printed book, and slips are small errors.

clue.text: Cover for embarrassment when gaffe left one reeling

indicators.note: reeling means staggering about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the usual abbreviation for left
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone left reeling by a social blunder looks for a way to hide their embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fig leaf covers nakedness in old paintings, and figuratively it is any flimsy concealment of something shameful.

clue.text: Get shot of Casanova giving out tips for the papacy

indicators.note: giving out the tips means letting go of the end letters of the words before

parts.note: to see off a rival is to get rid of them
a Romeo is a great lover, like Casanova

explanation.surface: A womaniser is thrown out of the Vatican for leaking secrets to the press.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces lose their last letter: SEE OF(f) and ROME(o) give SEE OF ROME.
explanation.definitionFit: The See of Rome is the bishopric of the Pope, so it is a formal name for the papacy itself.

clue.text: Easy job, turning over small bit of turf

indicators.note: turning something over flips it end to end, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A gardener's light task of flipping a small piece of lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: A doss is British slang for an undemanding task; 'Easy job' is a noun phrase, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a doss is a task needing no effort, the same as a cushy, easy job.

clue.text: Filthy rich nob means to have air travel for life

definitions.text: means to have air travel for life

indicators.note: something filthy is messed up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A very wealthy toff can afford to fly for the rest of his days.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'means' as money and 'air travel' as flying; really the air is breath travelling to the lungs.
explanation.definitionFit: The bronchi are the two main airways branching into the lungs, the channels breath passes through to keep us alive.

clue.text: Bouncer intends to grab Yankee, certainly

indicators.note: grabbing something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a ball is something that bounces
Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet
to mean to do something is to intend it

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman plans to seize an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' suggests a doorman; here it is anything that bounces.
explanation.definitionFit: 'By all means' is an idiom of willing agreement, used just like 'certainly' in reply to a request.

clue.text: Workplace doing away with cold drinks store

indicators.note: doing away with something removes it, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: an office is a place of work
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An office scraps chilled drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: OFFICE minus C. An offie is British slang for an off-licence, a shop selling alcohol to take away.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-licence is a British shop licensed to sell alcohol, and offie is its slang name.

clue.text: Got around and about jogging, initially shouted encouragement?

parts.note: ca is short for circa, about

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the first letter of jogging
to cry ole, as at a bullfight, is to shout encouragement

explanation.surface: A spectator went round cheering on runners.
explanation.walkthrough: OLED is the past tense of ole, cried in support; the question mark admits the verb is invented.
explanation.definitionFit: To cajole someone is to coax them, and getting around someone means winning them over by persuasion.

clue.text: If you ask me to dance, I'm bony, alright!

indicators.note: dancing moves things about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
OK means alright

explanation.surface: A skinny person, invited to dance, says they are fine with it.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In my book' is an idiom meaning in my opinion, the same as prefacing a view with 'if you ask me'.

clue.text: Teased by personnel, getting stick for heraldry

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them
staff are the personnel of a firm

explanation.surface: A worker who was mocked by colleagues gets told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting stick' looks like being criticised; the stick is the definition, a heraldic one.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragged staff is a heraldic charge, a branch with stubs of lopped twigs, famous in the Warwick bear and ragged staff.

clue.text: An essential part of the WI?

definitions.text: An essential part of the WI?

parts.words: An essential part of the WI?
parts.note: surface reading: a key component of the Women's Institute, or of the West Indies
setter's reading: the Women's Institute is famous for making preserves, and Jamaica begins with these letters in the West Indies

explanation.walkthrough: The WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's community group known for its fruit preserves ('jam and Jerusalem'); the answer also starts Jamaica in the West Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: Homemade fruit preserve is the stereotypical product of the Women's Institute, whose image is summed up as 'Jam and Jerusalem'.

clue.text: Drivers do get cross

definitions.meaning: first meaning: golfers using drivers hit the opening shot from a peg
second meaning: to become angry, in slang

explanation.walkthrough: Drivers suggests motorists losing their tempers; it is the golf club. The second sense is British slang for losing your temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers swing a driver to begin a hole, and in slang a person who blows up in anger is said to do the same.

clue.text: American music group's good general beat

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general
to club someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: A US band's drummer is a fine general beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A glee club is a choir, especially at an American school or college, singing short choral songs.

clue.text: Wonderful places to retire before death, old and useless

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: to put something is to place it
death is the end
O is the abbreviation for old
US stands for unserviceable, that is useless

explanation.surface: Choosing great retirement spots before you die, when you are old and of no use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Places to retire' suggests retirement homes; really 'places' is a verb and 'to retire' sends it backwards. US for useless is short for unserviceable.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupendous means astonishingly impressive, so it is a near synonym for wonderful.

clue.text: Fine memory game involving the Bible, starting at Genesis?

indicators.note: something involving another takes it in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
read-only memory in a computer
the Word is a name for scripture
go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A Bible-based memory game that begins with the first book.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis is the Bible's first book but also means a beginning, which is what the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: 'From the word go' is an idiom for right from the beginning, and genesis means origin.

clue.text: Go too far in some of test, maybe, attracting jeer

parts.note: overs are sets of six balls, and many make up a Test match in cricket
to hoot is to jeer

explanation.surface: A cricketer who goes overboard during a Test match draws boos from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a top-level international cricket match, bowled in overs of six balls each.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshoot is to go beyond a target, which is exactly going too far.

clue.text: Ill-feeling as a friend buttons lip

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to button something up is to close it in, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: cony is an obsolete term of endearment in Chambers; the setter seems to have meant crony
the lip of a cup is its rim

explanation.surface: Bad blood arises when a pal tells someone to shut up.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's error, confirmed by the Times crossword editor: the natural word for friend leaves an extra letter, so only an obsolete endearment fits. The online clue was later changed to 'holds back note'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is bitter resentment between people, a strong form of ill-feeling.

clue.text: Reporter at Stade de France in time to follow match

parts.note: things that correspond match each other
en is the French word for in
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A journalist at the Paris national stadium arrives on time to cover the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' sends EN and T after the match piece. The Stade de France is a reference only to signal French.
explanation.definitionFit: A correspondent is a journalist who reports on a particular subject or place, such as a sports correspondent.

clue.text: Check traveller getting on ship

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is a commercial traveller
re means about, on the subject of
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A sea passenger's embarkation is checked.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress a feeling is to hold it back, and to check something is to restrain it.

clue.text: Bond, not so informally dressed?

parts.note: a tie is a bond
less means minus, without

explanation.surface: James Bond, rarely seen dressed down.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond suggests the spy who is always in a dinner jacket; it is just a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Going without a necktie is the mark of casual dress, so a tieless man is dressed informally.

clue.text: Maiden in fairy tale getting highly emotional

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a fairy tale is a story
M for maiden, an over with no runs in cricket

explanation.surface: A girl in a fairy story becomes overwrought.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormy describes turbulent passions, as in a stormy relationship full of high emotion.

clue.text: Oscar and Carol after mischief in August

parts.note: an imp, a mischievous child, is a little mischief
Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet
to carol is to sing

explanation.surface: Two people, Oscar and Carol, get up to pranks during the summer month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' looks like the month; it is the adjective meaning dignified, and 'Carol' is a verb, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: An august person or building inspires awe and respect, which is what imposing means.

clue.text: Radioactive element blows up, causing confusion

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to fan is to blow air on something
U is the symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A nuclear reactor explodes and causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blows up' looks like an explosion, but up only turns FANS round. Snafu is military slang for a chaotic mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Snafu, from a military acronym, is a chaotic muddle, which is confusion.

clue.text: Verbal agreement resulting in promotion

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so the word is wanted by its sound

parts.note: assent is agreement

explanation.surface: A spoken agreement leads to a job promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a rise, and a promotion is a rise in rank.

clue.text: Nerve of elite military force

parts.note: the Special Air Service, the British special forces regiment
'of' is the possessive, written 's

explanation.surface: The courage of an elite army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read as SAS's, the force's. Sass is cheeky impudence, so nerve in the sense of gall.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve can mean cheeky boldness, and sass is impudent backchat.

clue.text: Have to pay for when not there, oddly

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are missing, leaving only the even ones

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Being charged for a period when you were absent seems strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To owe money is to be under an obligation to pay it.

clue.text: A short plain-spoken Party Conference perhaps bearing fruit

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter of the next word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
vocal means outspoken
a do is a party
Conference is a popular British variety of pear

explanation.surface: A brief, blunt political party conference that achieves results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party Conference' reads as a political gathering, but Conference is a pear variety and the party a do.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is a fruit, and avocado pear is its older, fuller name.

clue.text: Consents, with conditions, to work set by us

indicators.note: putting letters to work makes them into something new by rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone agrees, on certain terms, to a task we have set.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes-but is a grudging agreement followed by an objection, so it is consent hedged with conditions.

clue.text: Meet flying fist for one is boxing

indicators.note: boxing something means enclosing it as in a box

parts.note: say means for example, as does for one

indicators.note: a flying object is in wild motion, so these letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boxer's flying fist meets an opponent in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet' is a verb meaning fulfil, as in meeting a need; SAY boxes the shuffled fist.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy a requirement is to meet it, fulfilling what is demanded.
